identity.author: John Davenant
identity.work: Two Dissertations (De praedestinatione through Cap. X Arg. III)
identity.edition: Dissertationes duae (Cambridge: Roger Daniel, 1650). Partial through Cap. X Arg. III (Jacob/Esau / in-life consequences). Further Cap. X Args remain.

scope.locus: De praedestinatione Cap. X Arg. II+ / Arg. III.
scope.next_locus: Cap. X Arg. IV+ (continue confirmation of non-election from mere will).

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. I/II: reprobates rejected from the elect's grace not from foreseen final unbelief, but as lying in Adam's common sin — Arminius himself puts common sin before election/preterition, not final unbelief
english: And that rejection is not from their foreseen unbelief or final impenitence, but inasmuch as they are considered lying in Adam's common sin. Nay, Arminius himself, in the Collation with Junius, contends that what must be presupposed to election and preterition is not final unbelief or impenitence, but that sin in which all are commonly conceived. Nor does he dare make that the cause why God passes some over — only why he can pass some over (Pag. 96).
sections.latin: Idque non ex praevisa eorundem infidelitate aut impoenitentia finali, sed quatenus considerantur in communi Adae peccato jacentes. Quinetiam ipse Arminius in Collatione cum Junio, non infidelitatem aut impoenitentiam finalem, sed peccatum illud in quo omnes communiter concepti sunt, contendit praesupponendum esse electioni et praeteritioni: neque illud audet ponere causam cur Deus aliquos praetereat, sed solummodo cur aliquos praeterire possit, Pag. 96.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. II: Arminius's Exam of Perkins — some get only sufficient grace with foresight it will be rejected; elect get efficacious grace with foresight they will believe; God decreed not to give efficacious grace to some by reprobation
english: But now in his Examination of Perkins's Predestination (pag. 57 etc.), from Augustine's mind — and perhaps Scripture's sense, as he himself says — he acknowledges this: to some men, from the providence decree, only sufficient grace is administered, with God's certain forescience that free choice will reject it; to others, from the predestination decree, not only sufficient grace but efficacious, with God's certain forescience that by that grace's benefit those to whom it is fitted and applied will in fact will, believe, and be converted. A little later: God established not to give this efficacious grace to certain ones — and that by the reprobation decree.
sections.latin: Jam vero in Examine Praedestinationis Perkinsianae, pag. 57. etc. ex mente Augustini, forte et Scripturae sensu (sic enim ipse loquitur) agnoscit quibusdam hominibus ex decreto providentiae administrari gratiam tantummodo sufficientem, ac cum certa Dei praescientia quod sit rejicienda a libero hominis arbitrio; ex decreto autem praedestinationis administrari aliis non modo sufficientem gratiam, sed efficacem, cum certa Dei praescientia fore ut beneficio hujus gratiae reipsa velint, credant et convertantur illi quibus accommodatur et adhibetur. Paulo post: Deus hanc gratiam efficacem quibusdam non dare statuit, idque decreto reprobationis.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. II close: adversaries confess an inscrutable good pleasure in preparing/not preparing efficacious grace — that pleasure precedes forescience of faith accepted or grace finally rejected; they may not affirm the reverse
english: You see what the adversaries themselves confess. From that let us conclude: in preparing and not preparing efficacious grace there is a secret, inscrutable good pleasure of God. It does not follow forescience of faith and accepted grace in the elect, or forescience of unbelief and grace finally rejected in the reprobate — it precedes both. For it would be ridiculous to say that from the providence decree only sufficient grace is prepared for some, with certain forescience it will be rejected, and that from the reprobation decree efficacious grace — which no hard heart refuses — is denied them, and then to teach that this happens because God foresaw they would reject his grace and die in unbelief and pertinacity. Those who dare not deny the first ought not so confidently to have affirmed the second.
sections.latin: Videtis quid ipsi adversarii fateantur: ex quibus concludamus, esse in praeparanda et non praeparanda gratia efficaci arcanum quoddam et inscrutabile beneplacitum Dei, quod non sequitur praescientiam fidei et gratiae acceptatae in electis, ac praescientiam infidelitatis et gratiae finaliter rejectae in reprobatis, sed utriusque praescientiam antecedit. Ridiculus enim fuerit qui diceret, ex decreto providentiae praeparari aliquibus gratiam solummodo sufficientem, cum praescientia certa quod rejicietur, atque iisdem ex decreto reprobationis negari gratiam efficacem, quae a nullo duro corde respuitur, ac postea doceret hoc fieri quia Deus praevidebat hosce gratiam suam rejecturos et in sua infidelitate et pertinacia morituros. Qui igitur prius non audent negare, non debuerunt posterius tam confidenter affirmare.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. III: if reprobation hung on foreseen final impenitence/unbelief, no one would be reprobated except considered as dying — even as dead — because final perseverance/pertinacity is not fulfilled while we still live
english: Suppose the reprobation decree hung on the reprobates' foreseen final impenitence and unbelief. Then no one would be reprobated except as God considered him dying — nay, dead. Why is that plain? Because while life is lived here, neither anyone's final perseverance in faith, nor final pertinacity in unbelief, is fulfilled. Whatever comes before the end is only a step by which one climbs toward the summit, not the term by which the height's top is already held.
sections.latin: Si decretum reprobationis penderet ex praevisa finali impoenitentia et infidelitate reprobatorum, tum nemo reprobaretur nisi consideratus a Deo ut moribundus, imo ut mortuus. Ratio perspicua est; Quia dum hic vivitur, neque finalis cujusquam perseverantia in fide, neque finalis pertinacia in infidelitate adimpletur. Quicquid enim ante finem fuerit, gradus est quo ad fastigium ascenditur, non terminus quo jam culminis summa teneatur.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. III: election and rejection of Jacob and Esau depicted not after life's course but before birth, when they had done neither good nor evil (Rom. ix. 11–13) — so neither elected nor rejected from Arminian foresight
english: But that election and reprobation should first look on men as dead, or at least as at their last extremity, is unheard-of — and plainly contrary to Scripture and reason. Scripture depicts Jacob and Esau's election and rejection not as considered after both had run this life's course, but when they were not yet born and had done nothing yet of good or evil (Rom. ix. 11–13). Of those of whom one is elected without considering any good he antecedently rendered, and the other rejected without considering any actual sin he antecedently committed, it is plain neither was ante-elected or rejected from this Arminian foresight.
sections.latin: At electionem et reprobationem prius spectare homines qua mortuos, vel saltem qua in extremis positos, inauditum est, et sacris Scripturis ac rationi plane contrarium. Scripturae electionem et rejectionem Jacobi et Esavi nobis depingunt, non considerandam post decursum hujus vitae spatium ab utroque; sed cum nondum nascerentur, et nihil adhuc boni aut mali fecissent, Rom. ix. 11, 12, 13. Quorum vero unus eligitur absque consideratione ullius boni, ab eo antecedenter praestiti, alter rejicitur absque consideratione peccati alicujus actualis antecedenter ab eo perpetrati, illorum neutrum ex hac praevisione Arminiana anteelectum fuisse aut rejectum, liquido constat.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. III: even if Rom. ix is read only of temporal honor of Jacob over Esau, by theologians' consent Paul introduced it to represent eternal predestination/reprobation — not from contrary merits of works
english: I know some will not grant that those Apostolic words refer to Jacob and Esau's eternal predestination and reprobation — only to that purpose by which God of his good pleasure established to honor Jacob and subject Esau to him, at least in both their posterities. Be it so. Still, from theologians' consent and from the Apostle's whole discourse, this is clear: Paul introduced that example at least to represent the mystery of eternal predestination and reprobation, and to prove by argument from figure to thing figured that neither election of men to everlasting salvation, nor reprobation, is from contrary merits of works — but that God, of the sole choice of his will, elects some to salvation and reprobates others.
sections.latin: Scio nonnullos minime concedere praedicta Apostoli verba ad aeternam praedestinationem et reprobationem Jacobi et Esavi esse referenda, sed solummodo ad illud propositum quo constituit Deus pro beneplacito suo honorare Jacobum, et subjicere illi Esavum, saltem in posteris utriusque. Sit ita: Tamen ex consensu Theologorum, et ex toto discursu Apostoli illud liquet, hoc exemplum fuisse introductum a Paulo saltem ad repraesentandum aeternae praedestinationis et reprobationis mysterium, atque demonstrandum argumento a figura ad rem figuratam, neque electionem hominum ad aeternam salutem, neque reprobationem esse ex contrariis operum meritis, sed Deum ex solo voluntatis suae arbitrio alios eligere ad salutem, alios autem reprobare.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. III close: reprobation does not fall on men only after they are considered to have persevered in sins to the last breath — many consequences of reprobation reach them in this life's course
english: But we confirm the Minor still more openly: reprobation does not fall on men only after they are considered to have persevered in their sins to the last breath. Many consequences of reprobation belong to the reprobate while they are set in this life's course — denial of efficacious grace or of calling according to purpose; permission of the wicked to go on here in their sins unpunished; delivering them over to a reprobate mind. These and the like.
sections.latin: Sed adhuc apertius confirmamus Minorem, nempe, Reprobationem non cadere in homines postquam ad extremum halitum in peccatis suis perseverasse considerantur; Quia multa consequentia reprobationis pertinent ad reprobatos in hujus vitae cursu constitutos; qualia sunt negatio gratiae efficacis sive vocationis secundum propositum, permissio improborum ut impune pergant hic in peccatis suis, traditio eorundem in reprobum sensum. Haec et alia hujusmodi.
